clusters.title: Slack Digest Alerts Fire Too Late
clusters.summary: Users report that Slack notification digests for newly surfaced feedback themes arrive hours after the underlying data has been processed, making real-time triage impossible. Product managers relying on Unwrap to catch urgent customer complaints before they escalate say the lag undermines the core value proposition of continuous intelligence.
verbatims: We set up the Slack integration specifically so our PM team would get alerted to spikes in negative sentiment, but the digest showed up 6 hours after the feedback had already been tagged and clustered in the dashboard — by then our CS team had already escalated the issue manually.

The Slack alerts for new insight clusters are supposed to keep me from having to log in constantly, but the delay is so inconsistent — sometimes 20 minutes, sometimes half a day — that I've stopped trusting them and just check the web app directly.

I love the concept of getting a daily digest of top themes pushed to our product channel, but when a critical bug complaint spikes in our NPS verbatims, I need to know within the hour, not at the end of the business day.

clusters.title: AI Theme Clusters Merge Unrelated Topics
clusters.summary: The automated clustering engine frequently groups semantically distinct feedback topics into a single theme, requiring manual splitting that users say defeats the purpose of automated analysis. Teams working with multi-product or multi-segment feedback sources find this especially painful because a bug report and a feature request about the same surface area get collapsed into one unactionable cluster.
verbatims: I had a cluster called 'Reporting' that Unwrap bundled together complaints about slow dashboard load times, requests for CSV export, and confusion about how metrics are calculated — those are three completely different engineering tasks and I had to manually re-label everything before I could route it to the right squad.

The AI is great at pulling feedback in from our Zendesk and Intercom sources, but when I look at the generated themes, billing complaints and onboarding confusion keep getting lumped together just because users mention 'getting started' in both contexts. Splitting clusters manually every week is tedious.

We integrated our G2 reviews and App Store data and the clustering picked up 'performance' as one giant bucket — it mixed iOS crash reports, slow API response complaints, and general 'the app feels sluggish' comments. I need sub-themes or confidence scores so I can triage properly.

clusters.title: Salesforce Integration Drops Custom Field Mappings
clusters.summary: Users who map Unwrap insight data to custom Salesforce fields report that the field mappings silently reset after platform updates, causing weeks of feedback metadata to land in the wrong CRM fields or get lost entirely. Because the failure is silent — no error notification is triggered — teams often discover the issue only during quarterly reviews when data looks anomalous.
verbatims: We spent two weeks carefully mapping our customer segment tags from Unwrap into our Salesforce opportunity fields so our sales team could see which accounts were flagging product gaps, and then an update just wiped the custom field config without any warning email or in-app alert.

The Salesforce connector works beautifully when it's set up correctly, but after the platform pushed an update in March our 'Product Area' custom field mapping broke and all new feedback synced into the default 'Description' field as raw text — we lost three weeks of properly tagged data.

I raised this with support and they confirmed it's a known issue with custom object mappings after version updates, but there's no changelog or heads-up when this will affect your instance. For a tool we're using to close the loop with enterprise accounts, that's a serious reliability gap.

clusters.title: Exported Reports Lose Hierarchy and Formatting
clusters.summary: When users export insight reports to PDF or CSV, the nested theme hierarchy — parent themes, sub-themes, and associated verbatim counts — collapses into a flat, unformatted list that is not shareable with executives or stakeholders. Users say they are forced to manually reconstruct the structure in PowerPoint or Google Slides, adding hours of work before each leadership review.
verbatims: The insights view inside Unwrap is genuinely impressive — I can see parent themes broken down by sentiment and source — but the moment I export to PDF for my VP of Product, it comes out as a flat bullet list with no visual hierarchy and the verbatim quotes lose their source attribution completely.

Every month before our product review I export the top feedback themes and spend 90 minutes reformatting the CSV in Google Sheets because the export doesn't preserve the sub-theme groupings or the percentage breakdowns by customer segment. The analysis is solid, the export is unusable.

I tried using the CSV export to pull theme data into our internal BI tool and the nested structure just flattened — sub-themes became separate rows with no parent ID column, so I had no way to reconstruct which clusters belonged together without going back into the UI manually.

clusters.title: High-Volume Sources Drown Out Smaller Channels
clusters.summary: When users connect both a high-volume source like Zendesk support tickets and a lower-volume source like NPS survey responses, the AI-generated themes skew almost entirely toward the dominant source, making signals from smaller but strategically important channels nearly invisible. Users want source-weighted or normalized analysis but currently have no configuration option to balance influence across connected data sources.
verbatims: We connected our Zendesk tickets, Typeform NPS responses, and App Store reviews, but because we have 10,000 support tickets and only 300 NPS responses, every top theme is essentially just support ticket analysis — the NPS verbatims that our C-suite cares most about are completely buried.

I specifically added our enterprise customer interview transcripts to get a strategic signal separate from the noise in our support volume, but Unwrap just treats all sources equally by raw count, so 5,000 tickets about password resets overwhelm the 40 interviews talking about missing API capabilities.

There needs to be a source weighting option or at minimum a filter to view themes by data source independently before seeing the blended view. Right now the blended analysis is only useful if all your sources have comparable volume, which is almost never true in practice.
